log.reply:
**Subject:** Executive Briefing proposal for Tamarack Instruments

Dana Whitfield,

**Situation**

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. Its AI use cases are a customer service chatbot deployed on the support portal, an AI visual inspection pilot on the German production line and AI sales forecasting planned for next year. An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded no inventory of AI systems. Your stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to start next year, on a date not yet fixed.

**What the Briefing covers for Tamarack Instruments**

The Briefing will map the EU AI Act and GDPR to each use case. This includes how the visual inspection system may be classified and what transparency expectations may apply to the chatbot. These are expectations to verify with counsel, not legal advice. United States requirements appear only as a general landscape item.

The readiness discussion starts from the June 2026 audit finding and explores how AI governance could connect with ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 9001 and internal audit. The operating model draws on the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). Board-layer material comes from AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

Three principles frame the session: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human. Under the last of these, every material outcome attaches to a named human owner with decision rights, oversight and the power to intervene. The Briefing will also place German works council consultation and EU residency of customer data within the governance sequence.

**Logistics and price**

The Executive Briefing runs 2 hours, live virtual, at US$3,000, for executive leadership and board-level attendees. The audience roles identified are General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. The session date is Unknown and will be agreed with you.

**What you receive afterward**

You will receive a written follow-up memo recording the decisions surfaced, readiness observations and three prioritized recommendations, each mapped to a further program option. The Briefing does not provide certification, audit outcomes or regulatory approval.

**Next step**

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. At intake we would like to confirm four points:

1. Where the chatbot is hosted.
2. Whether the chatbot processes customer personal data.
3. Whether the visual inspection pilot captures data about production staff.
4. Who owns each use case.

Please reply with two or three suitable dates.

Kind regards,
AI Governance Academy

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

"ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to start next year" adds "expected" to the block's "work to start next year". I treated this as a faithful restatement, since the confidence note already says the start date is not fixed.

The "What you receive afterward" section describes a follow-up memo, which is program content rather than a Client fact. I treated it as proposed work. This is consistent with the checklist's allowance for Client-facing Mode A content.
